note: Pinned revisions of the sibling repositories sb3-creator's cross-repo gates consume. CI checks these exact commits out beside the repo (.github/workflows/ci.yml) so the gates RUN rather than skip; test/helpers/siblings.mjs turns an absent sibling into a failure when CI=true. Update a pin deliberately, in its own commit, with the suite green against it. `rev` MUST be the FULL 40-character SHA: actions/checkout only recognises a full SHA as a commit, and turns anything shorter into `git fetch origin +refs/heads/<ref>*` — a branch glob that matches nothing. An abbreviated pin here took every CI run on main down at the checkout step, before lint, tests, the mutation prover or the build ran at all. gate-integrity asserts the length; `revShort` exists only for prose.

bw-board.why: the device/board simulator the gallery e2e and physics gates drive. Advanced from 1caf851 (which took the STM32F030 light tier and deliberately stopped short of the attiny88 pa0->gnd2 rename) to master's tip after the defect wave: D18 op-amp secant convergence (999eb66/187694f — the LM358 now realises 1 + Rf/Rg = 46.4545455545 at every input instead of a damped 31.06, which is the whole of 76-multimeter's A-mode arithmetic), D20 output limiting (18555e7/5abf9ea, GATED: spec-updates/opamp-output-limit.md + oracles in the same commit, rout + iShort 40 mA), D23 first-solve capacitor semantics (f87adcc), the capture:'sample' scope channels (9441e4f/2169d9b), the bargraph that never lit and was not a diode (3c7cbe8), and the attiny88 pin-22 rename (e1bda3f) whose 135-circuit re-seat is carried on the cui side by TERMINAL_ALIASES + migrateTerminals — measured here, not assumed: all 2162 corpus circuits load and the claim census is byte-identical either side of the bump. Corpus measured against exactly this pair: 2635 claims, compared 1239, mismatched 1 (the pre-existing arduino-sk-p04-color-mixing one) on 2026-08-29.

bw-circuit-ui.why: the canonical circuit model, engine, and the ONE wire-endpoint dialect reader the corpus gates read circuit.json through. Advanced from 06c7ea7 (the stm32f030-part commit) to master's tip: the attiny88 pa0->gnd2 migration on this side (be6361d + ea91228 — a saved terminals array is now resolved against what the engine offers NOW, which is what carries the 135 shipped circuits forward), D21 meter input impedance (3f1d194 — a meter is 10 MOhm and no longer empties the board), per-channel V/div and FFT (7696656), worker sweeps (134cad0), and fbe7338, which is the one to know about: engineKindFor tested `typeof eng.hasDevice === 'function'` and the engine has never exported hasDevice, so EVERY passthrough kind silently collapsed to a generic 'mcu'. With that fixed, a board kind reaches the solver as its registered device, and a board-kind device drives only the GPIO terminals the part DECLARES — which found six benches in this corpus whose uno1 declared `terminals: ["gnd2"]` while wiring D13/D9/A0/D2/D12, repaired in the same commit as this bump. Corpus measured against exactly this pair: 2635 claims, compared 1239, mismatched 1, identical to 1caf851+06c7ea7 claim for claim, on 2026-08-29. LEDGERED 2026-08-29 (fab-sbx), because this bump's entry named six commits and omitted the two seating-shaped ones, and their absence was later read as an unrecorded behaviour change in 60-retro-console and 61-console-pong. Both are accounted for and NEITHER moves this corpus. e58d528 ("A board that cannot be seated must not load as seated") drops a stored seat whose KIND has no breadboard footprint; its own commit message measures the blast radius as 61 of 9011 seated parts, ALL arduino_uno, and this corpus has none left seated because scripts/normalize-controller-seating.mjs already re-authored them. 01101a2 ("Placement that knows how big the part is") changes only the designer's empty-spot search, writes nothing persisted, and says in its own scope note that the path is an unreached fallback. VERDICT ON 60/61: ACCEPT — there was nothing to re-seat. Measured here at exactly this pair rather than inferred: all twelve circuit files of the two examples load, seat-on-disk equals seat-after-load on all six primary benches (dropped=[] for every one), and the nets are bb1:n-col-*. The three net-lgc-* nets in the pair are in the mega and stc12 VARIANTS only, joining arduino_mega to seven_seg_3 — two kinds with no breadboard footprint, so a logical net is the only correct answer, and the Mega has read `noseat` in every revision of that file. The flat twins drop their seats at load, which is fromJSON's pre-existing seat-without-a-breadboard rule and not this bump. What actually moved those benches' partitionShas was sb3-creator 33265cc, a part-id rename (mcu1 -> mega1 / stc151); the two variants whose id stayed mcu1 have unchanged shas, which is the control. The claim that they were unseated came from test/COVERAGE-ASSERT-PHYSICS.md, now RETRACTED: all 46 of its "no circuit file" rows are false and assert-physics passes both examples.
